description.value: The study compared neural correlates of passively viewing and actively decreasing emotional reactions to unpleasant moral and non-moral pictures using functional magnetic resonance imaging.

spans.text: The present study contrasted the neural correlates of passively viewing vs. actively decreasing emotional reactions to unpleasant pictures that either contained or did not contain moral violations.

value: We hypothesized that brain regions previously implicated in moral processing would be activated to a similar extent when viewing both moral and non-moral conditions.
we expected that the regulation of moral and non-moral emotions would also engage different brain regions than those involved in basic emotion regulation.

we predicted that the act of attempting to decrease emotional responses for moral and non-moral stimuli would elicit activity in reappraisal-related regions reported in previous studies ( ), and that morally relevant stimuli would engage additional processing in regions associated with resolving moral emotions.
We also predicted diminished limbic activation during regulation, reflecting the success of regulation processes in diminishing emotional responses.

description.value: Ten healthy right-handed female adults were scanned in an fMRI study with two scan runs and five trial types involving passive viewing or emotional regulation of moral and non-moral pictures and an odd-even baseline task.

spans.text: During scanning, subjects completed 20 28-s trials across 2 separate scan runs.
Each of the 5 trial types (Watch Moral/Non-Moral, Decrease Moral/Non-Moral, Odd–Even) was presented 4 times

spans.text: Two sets of color pictures (32 moral, 32 non-moral) were selected mostly from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS) ( ), and supplemented with pictures from the popular media.

Condition effects at the subject level were modeled by box-car regressors representing the occurrence of each of the 5 block types, convolved with a canonical hemodynamic response function for the 20-s period during which the subject either passively viewed or decreased their emotional responses to the pictures or performed the baseline task.

source_definition.value: The five experimental trial types were Watch Moral, Watch Non-Moral, Decrease Moral, Decrease Non-Moral, and Odd–Even baseline. The first four involved viewing or decreasing emotional responses to moral or non-moral pictures; the Odd–Even condition required covertly judging whether displayed numbers were odd or even.

model_settings.value: Group data were analyzed using a random-effects model. Individual subject data were analyzed using a fixed-effects model. Condition effects were modeled with box-car regressors convolved with a canonical hemodynamic response function; images were motion-corrected, normalized with SPM99, smoothed with a 6 mm FWHM Gaussian kernel, globally scaled, and high-pass filtered.

estimator.value: random effects at the group level; fixed effects at the individual-subject level
